A URL import needs internet, every single time you run it

file from the internet on every run. If you’re offline, or the URL moves,

5. The formula interface, immediately, on whatever you imported

children.label: 5. The formula interface, immediately, on whatever you imported

children.value:
Here’s the payoff for treating “import” as one destination regardless of
source: the instant you have a data frame — from

, a CSV, an
Excel sheet, or a URL — the same
works on it, no matter where it came from:

favstats(~ sleep_hours, data = survey)      # from the CSV
favstats(bill_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins)   # from the URL

taught you — “bill length, broken down by species” —
applied without a single change to a dataset you’d never seen a minute ago.
That reusability is the entire reason

’s formula grammar is worth
learning well: once it’s automatic, a brand-new dataset is never a barrier,
only the statistics is.
